title: Artificial Boolean Flags Used Only for Loop Exit
pattern: A local mutable boolean is tested in a loop condition and changed inside the loop solely to arrange termination on a later condition check.
why_bad: Artificial mutable state obscures exit points and requires readers to follow flag propagation through branches rather than reading direct structured control flow.
detection: Follow a local boolean from initialization through loop-header checks and assignments, including nested branches. Confirm that it conveys no program result or persistent state and is used only to govern loop termination.
counterexample: A flag representing actual program data needed after the loop is not merely an exit device. Direct break/return is already explicit. Shared cancellation flags and other externally meaningful state are not this local artificial-flag pattern.
source: Martin Fowler, *Refactoring*, "Remove Control Flag"; Trevor Foucher & Dustin Boswell, *The Art of Readable Code*, Chapter 9; Martin Fowler, Refactoring, p. 483-484 [483-484].
